A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ActiveSGM work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and supplements support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original ActiveSGM simulation results for semantic segmentation, reconstruction, rendering, component ablations and runtime on Replica and Matterport3D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the supplement. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The sparse top-k representation, semantic losses, keyframe strategy, exploration criteria and path planner are unchanged. Specifying that the entropy mask applies to pseudo-ground-truth predictions clarifies the existing loss rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight Replica scenes, four-scene ReplicaSLAM comparison subset and five MP3D scenes for the same mapping, segmentation and rendering tasks. The added explanation of simulation-based evaluation introduces no new test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every matched results table. The three baseline categories described in v2 reorganize existing comparisons, including passive SGS-SLAM, rather than adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, trajectories, budgets, metrics, sensor settings and preprocessing remain unchanged. v2 newly specifies that the existing passive SGS-SLAM comparison disables tracking and uses ground-truth poses; v1 states no conflicting setting, so this is additional documentation rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: The top-k and semantic-loss ablations, passive-versus-active comparison, color-coding analysis and runtime analysis are retained unchanged. v1 Table S.2 becomes v2 Table 2, and the existing KL-versus-Hellinger discussion moves into Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and scene averages without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Semantic entropy remains an algorithm component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All eight matched result tables retain identical entries and values. For example, Table 1 retains Replica mIoU of 84.89% at 777 steps and MP3D average IoU of 65.58%. The qualitative findings and dense-versus-sparse rendering times of 61 ms versus 3.1 ms also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) retain the same mathematical content; the parenthesis correction in Equation (7) is typographical. Perfect-localization and perfect-execution assumptions move from v1 Section S.2 to v2 Section 5 without substantive revision. No proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about active semantic Gaussian mapping, uncertainty-guided exploration, sparse semantic storage and robustness to noisy predictions. The claimed novelty and contribution scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains the simulation-only evaluation rationale and explicitly qualifies comparisons between SLAM systems and mapping with perfect localization. It removes v1's warning about unreliable semantic initialization in occluded regions. Other principal limitations are retained, partly through relocation from the supplement.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a repository link and stated availability. It also clarifies the entropy mask's input and the existing SGS-SLAM baseline's tracking and pose configuration. Hardware, fine-tuning budgets, rendering pseudocode and asset licenses remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds 'Active perception using neural radiance fields' as reference 60 and expands the discussion distinguishing trajectory planning from next-best-view selection and describing mutual-information-based semantic exploration. The existing cited works remain, largely with renumbered references.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the evaluation narrative and comparison headings. Existing assumptions and ablation discussion move into the main text, while the supplement is reorganized around implementation, results and reproducibility. Front matter and acknowledgments also change, but the overall narrative and most method prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing ablation table moves from v1 Table S.2 to main-text Table 2, with corresponding table renumbering and page reflow. Figure 1 expands the exploration-criterion labels, and the author block is compacted. No new empirical figures or tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing comparisons easier to assess through explicit localization caveats and clearer baseline documentation, and provides concrete code-access information. Moving ablations and assumptions into the main text improves their visibility. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the occluded-region initialization warning; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
